insight: Japan's performance in the 2026 World Cup shows that hydration breaks have a significant impact on their momentum, with the team gaining momentum in 5 out of 8 breaks, indicating a slight overall improvement in their gameplay after these pauses. However, when Japan was pressing before a hydration break, they tended to lose momentum, with an average change of -0.075 minutes, only managing to maintain their momentum in 2 out of 4 instances. In contrast, when Japan was not pressing before a break, they were able to maintain their momentum, with no average change in their performance, suggesting that the team is better able to regroup and refocus when not under intense pressure. This data suggests that Japan's coaches may need to adjust their strategy during hydration breaks, particularly when the team is pressing, to minimize losses in momentum and capitalize on the brief pause in play.
